prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-04-23, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-04-23):
| Current ratio           | 1.39 |
| Retained earnings       | 0M |
| Current liabilities     | 22,085M |
| Current assets          | 30,590M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 21,312M |
| Total liabilities       | 52,676M |
| Total assets            | 73,988M |
| EBIT / operating income | 886M |
| Revenue                 | 9,143M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows solid liquidity (current ratio 1.39) but elevated leverage (total liabilities 52,676m vs total assets 73,988m; debt-to-assets ~0.71; debt-to-equity ~2.46) and no retained earnings, implying limited cushion against earnings volatility. Profitability is modest (EBIT margin ~9.7%), but absence of retained earnings and higher leverage suggest moderate credit risk. Overall, credit quality aligns with one-notch below investment grade, but not at the high-risk end.

DECISION: BBB+
